observations.value: The opacity in Figure 1 (right hilar/upper lobe) is present and indistinct; in Figure 2 it is completely absent; in Figure 3 it reappears in the identical anatomical location with similar shape and indistinct margins. The recurrence is precisely at the same site.

observations.attribute: presence of volume loss or mediastinal shift indicating obstructive atelectasis
observations.value: In Figure 3 (and its crop), there is no clear elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, tracheal shift to the right, or rib crowding to suggest significant volume loss. However, subtle collapse cannot be definitively excluded from these 2D CXRs alone.
Figure 2 shows normal lung parenchyma in the right upper lobe/hilar region with no residual opacity, confirming documented resolution.

hypotheses.name: Obstructive lesion (e.g., endobronchial tumor) causing recurrent post-obstructive pneumonia
hypotheses.basis: Identical-location recurrence after full resolution strongly suggests an underlying obstructive cause rather than incomplete treatment or new infection. Heavy smoking is a major risk factor for bronchogenic carcinoma, which commonly presents as recurrent pneumonia in the same segment due to endobronchial obstruction.

hypotheses.name: Endobronchial fibrolipoma or mucus plug
hypotheses.basis: These can cause recurrent obstructive pneumonia in the same location; however, fibrolipomas are rare and typically occur in younger patients without smoking history, and mucus plugs usually resolve with therapy unless chronic (e.g., in CF or asthma), which is not indicated here.

uncertainties: Absence of CT imaging prevents definitive characterization of the hilar mass or bronchial narrowing.
No sputum or biopsy data to confirm microbiology or malignancy.
Subtle volume loss or bronchial cutoff signs may be missed on 2D CXR; lateral view helps but is insufficient for bronchial detail.

and cannot prove existence, physical size or interval change.
